questions.question: Statistical modeling involves:

options.B: Using mathematical equations and probability to represent real-world data relationships
options.C: Graphical design of spreadsheets

questions.explanation: Using mathematical equations and probability to represent real-world data relationships. Explanation: Statistical models use equations to represent patterns in data, enabling prediction and analysis of real-world phenomena.

questions.question: Correlation between two variables means:

options.A: One variable directly causes the other to change
options.B: There is a perfect mathematical relationship
options.C: A statistical relationship — they tend to change together
options.D: They have the same mean value

questions.explanation: A statistical relationship — they tend to change together. Explanation: Correlation measures the strength and direction of a statistical relationship. It does NOT imply causation.

questions.question: A random sample is important in statistics because:

options.A: It is the largest possible sample
options.B: It reduces processing time
options.C: It gives every member of the population an equal chance of selection, reducing bias

questions.explanation: It gives every member of the population an equal chance of selection, reducing bias. Explanation: Random sampling is the foundation of representative statistics — it minimises sampling bias and allows generalisation to the population.

questions.question: Summary statistics include all of the following EXCEPT:

options.B: Median
options.C: Standard deviation

questions.explanation: Primary key. Explanation: Primary key is a database concept. Summary statistics include measures of central tendency (mean, median, mode) and spread (range, standard deviation).

questions.question: An outlier in a dataset is:

options.B: The middle value when sorted
options.C: A data point significantly different from the rest of the data

questions.explanation: A data point significantly different from the rest of the data. Explanation: Outliers are extreme values far from the general pattern — they can significantly distort the mean.

questions.question: A positive correlation between two variables means:

options.A: When one increases, the other decreases
options.B: They are completely unrelated
options.C: When one increases, the other also tends to increase

questions.explanation: When one increases, the other also tends to increase. Explanation: Positive correlation: both variables move in the same direction (e.g., more study hours leads to higher exam scores).

questions.question: The mean of the dataset {4, 8, 6, 5, 7} is:
Which measure of central tendency is most affected by extreme outliers?

options.B: Median
options.C: Mean

questions.explanation: Mean. Explanation: The mean uses all values in its calculation — one extreme outlier can pull it far from the centre of the data.

questions.question: Data visualization tools are used in data analysis primarily to:

options.B: Encrypt sensitive records
options.C: Present data patterns and trends in a visual, interpretable format

questions.explanation: Present data patterns and trends in a visual, interpretable format. Explanation: Charts, graphs, and dashboards reveal patterns invisible in raw numbers, making insights accessible to non-technical audiences.

questions.question: What does standard deviation measure?

options.B: The most frequent value
options.C: The spread of values around the mean
options.D: The difference between the maximum and minimum

questions.explanation: The spread of values around the mean. Explanation: Low standard deviation means values are clustered tightly around the mean. High standard deviation means values are widely dispersed.

questions.question: The median of the dataset {3, 7, 2, 9, 5} when sorted is:
questions.explanation: 5. Explanation: Sorted: {2, 3, 5, 7, 9}. The middle value (position 3 of 5) is 5.

questions.question: A negative correlation between two variables means:

options.B: When one increases, the other tends to decrease
options.C: Both decrease simultaneously

questions.explanation: When one increases, the other tends to decrease. Explanation: Negative correlation: the variables move in opposite directions (e.g., more absences leads to lower grades).

questions.question: Which Python library provides DataFrame structures for data analysis?

options.B: Matplotlib
options.C: Pandas

questions.explanation: Pandas. Explanation: Pandas provides the DataFrame — a 2D labelled data structure like a spreadsheet — and powerful tools for data manipulation and analysis.

questions.question: Causation differs from correlation because causation:

options.B: Means one variable directly and reliably produces a change in the other
options.C: Only applies to negative relationships

questions.explanation: Means one variable directly and reliably produces a change in the other. Explanation: Correlation is a statistical relationship; causation requires controlled evidence that one variable directly drives the other.

questions.question: Which chart type is best suited for showing how a value changes over time?

options.B: Bar chart
options.C: Line graph

questions.explanation: Line graph. Explanation: Line graphs connect data points chronologically — ideal for visualising trends, growth, and changes over a time period. Questions 16–30: Expanded Questions ★

questions.question: In a linear regression model y = mx + b, what does 'b' represent? ★

options.B: The dependent variable
options.C: The y-intercept — where the line crosses the y-axis

questions.explanation: The y-intercept — where the line crosses the y-axis. Explanation: In the linear equation y = mx + b, 'm' is the slope (rate of change) and 'b' is the y- intercept, which is the value of y when x equals zero — the point where the line meets the y-axis.

questions.question: In supervised learning, a labeled dataset means: ★

options.A: The data has no categories or classifications
options.B: Each data point comes with a known correct answer or category
options.C: The algorithm works without any prior data

questions.explanation: Each data point comes with a known correct answer or category. Explanation: Supervised learning trains an algorithm using labeled data — data that already has the correct output attached. The model learns to map inputs to outputs by comparing its predictions to these known labels.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of unsupervised learning? ★

options.A: Predicting whether an email is spam or not
options.B: Classifying fruit images as 'Fruit' or 'Not Fruit'
options.C: Grouping customers into clusters based on purchasing behaviour
options.D: Forecasting next month's sales using historical data

questions.explanation: Grouping customers into clusters based on purchasing behaviour. Explanation: Unsupervised learning finds patterns in unlabeled data without being told the correct answer. Clustering groups similar data points together — no predefined labels are used.

questions.question: What is the purpose of data wrangling in a data science case study? ★

options.A: Collecting raw data from the internet
options.B: Presenting final results to stakeholders
options.C: Cleaning, transforming, and preparing raw data into a usable format

questions.explanation: Cleaning, transforming, and preparing raw data into a usable format. Explanation: Data wrangling involves removing duplicates, filling missing values, and transforming raw data into a clean, structured format that is suitable for analysis and modeling.

questions.question: Which of the following is a data science use case approach used for predicting future values? ★

options.B: Forecasting
options.C: Association

questions.explanation: Forecasting. Explanation: Forecasting is a common data science approach that uses historical data and statistical models to predict future values — for example, weather prediction, stock prices, or sales trends.

questions.question: The principle of randomization in experimental design ensures: ★

options.A: All participants receive the same treatment
options.B: Groups are formed without bias by randomly assigning participants
options.C: The experiment is repeated multiple times

questions.explanation: Groups are formed without bias by randomly assigning participants. Explanation: Randomization prevents systematic bias in group formation. By randomly assigning participants to treatment and control groups, any differences in outcomes can be attributed to the treatment rather than pre-existing group differences.

questions.question: What is a control group in experimental design? ★

options.A: The group that receives the most effective treatment
options.B: The group that is given no treatment, used as a baseline for comparison
options.C: The group with the largest sample size
options.D: The group selected by the researcher personally

questions.explanation: The group that is given no treatment, used as a baseline for comparison. Explanation: A control group receives no treatment (or the standard treatment) and serves as a reference point. Comparing the treatment group's results against the control group isolates the effect of the variable being tested.

questions.question: What does the principle of replication in experimental design guarantee? ★

options.A: All data is encrypted before use
options.B: Results are reproducible and not due to chance or coincidence
options.C: Only one group is used in the experiment
options.D: Data is collected from a single source

questions.explanation: Results are reproducible and not due to chance or coincidence. Explanation: Replication requires repeating an experiment multiple times, possibly with different groups. Consistent results across repetitions confirm that findings are reliable and not simply a coincidence or random occurrence.

questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes a parameter from a statistic? ★

options.A: A parameter describes a sample; a statistic describes a population
options.B: A parameter describes an entire population; a statistic describes a sample
options.C: Parameters and statistics are identical concepts
options.D: Statistics are always more accurate than parameters

questions.explanation: A parameter describes an entire population; a statistic describes a sample. Explanation: A parameter is a fixed value describing a whole population (usually unknown). A statistic is a calculated value from a sample that estimates the parameter. For example, the average income of all Pakistanis is a parameter; the average income of 1,000 surveyed Pakistanis is a statistic.

questions.question: What is A/B testing, as used by companies like Facebook and YouTube? ★

options.A: A method to encrypt user data using two algorithms
options.B: Comparing two versions of a feature with different user groups to determine which performs better
options.C: A backup strategy using two separate servers
options.D: A way to compress data using binary encoding

questions.explanation: Comparing two versions of a feature with different user groups to determine which performs better. Explanation: A/B testing (split testing) involves showing version A to one randomly assigned group and version B to another, then comparing performance metrics to make data-driven decisions about which version to implement.

questions.question: In the context of K-means clustering, what does 'clustering' mean? ★

options.B: Labeling each data point with a predefined category
options.C: Grouping data points with maximum similarities together

questions.explanation: Grouping data points with maximum similarities together. Explanation: K-means clustering is an unsupervised learning algorithm that divides data into k groups (clusters) where members within each cluster are as similar to each other as possible and as different from other clusters as possible.

questions.question: Which primary data collection method involves asking a group of people with something in common to share their opinions? ★

options.B: Survey
options.C: Oral history

questions.explanation: Focus group. Explanation: A focus group is an in-depth discussion conducted with a selected group of participants who share common characteristics. It provides richer qualitative insight than surveys but has drawbacks like lack of privacy and potential domination by one participant.

questions.question: Secondary data collection differs from primary data collection in that secondary data: ★

options.B: Has already been collected by someone else for a different purpose
options.C: Is only available from government archives

questions.explanation: Has already been collected by someone else for a different purpose. Explanation: Secondary data is pre-existing data collected by other researchers, organisations, or government bodies. It is faster and cheaper to obtain than primary data but may not perfectly match the current research needs.

questions.question: What is the relationship between correlation and causation? ★

options.A: Causation always implies correlation, but correlation does not imply causation
options.B: Correlation always implies causation
options.C: They are the same thing

questions.explanation: Causation always implies correlation, but correlation does not imply causation. Explanation: If X causes Y, then X and Y will always be correlated. However, two variables can be correlated simply by coincidence or because a third variable affects both — this does not mean one causes the other.

questions.question: Which Python command is used to install the Pandas library for data analysis? ★

options.B: load pandas
options.C: pip install pandas

questions.explanation: pip install pandas. Explanation: pip is Python's package manager. 'pip install pandas' downloads and installs the Pandas library along with all its dependencies, making it available for import in Python programs.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of data visualization? ★

options.A: To store raw data in a compressed format
options.B: To represent data graphically so trends and patterns can be easily understood
options.C: To encrypt sensitive business data

questions.explanation: To represent data graphically so trends and patterns can be easily understood. Explanation: Data visualization converts raw numbers into charts, graphs, and maps, making it easier for both technical and non-technical audiences to identify trends, outliers, and patterns in large datasets.

questions.question: Which chart type is most appropriate for comparing proportions of a whole? ★

options.B: Bar chart
options.C: Pie chart

questions.explanation: Pie chart. Explanation: A pie chart divides a circle into slices representing each category's proportion of the total. It is best used when comparing parts of a whole, such as market share or budget allocation.

questions.question: What type of chart is best for comparing values across multiple categories? ★

options.B: Pie chart
options.C: Bar chart

questions.explanation: Bar chart. Explanation: Bar charts use rectangular bars of varying lengths to compare values across different categories side by side. They are ideal for discrete comparisons such as sales by product or population by region.

questions.question: In data analysis, what does 'data exploration' involve? ★

options.A: Deleting irrelevant rows from a database
options.B: Initially examining the dataset to understand its structure, patterns, and anomalies
options.C: Writing final conclusions for a report
options.D: Uploading data to a cloud server

questions.explanation: Initially examining the dataset to understand its structure, patterns, and anomalies. Explanation: Data exploration is the first step in analysis — it involves looking at the data's shape, distributions, missing values, and relationships to understand what it contains before applying any formal analysis or modeling.

questions.question: What is a data product? ★

options.A: A physical storage device containing raw data
options.B: A tool or application that uses data analysis results to deliver value or automate decisions
options.C: A type of spreadsheet formula
options.D: A method of collecting survey responses

questions.explanation: A tool or application that uses data analysis results to deliver value or automate decisions. Explanation: A data product leverages the outputs of data analysis to provide real-time recommendations, automate business processes, or deliver data-driven services — for example, a recommendation engine or fraud detection system.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the mode of a dataset? ★

options.A: The arithmetic average of all values
options.B: The middle value when data is sorted
options.C: The value that appears most frequently
options.D: The difference between the highest and lowest values

questions.explanation: The value that appears most frequently. Explanation: The mode is the value that occurs most often in a dataset. A dataset can have one mode (unimodal), two modes (bimodal), or more. It is the only measure of central tendency applicable to categorical data.

questions.question: In the linear regression equation y = mx + b, which variable represents the independent variable? ★

options.B: b
options.C: m

questions.explanation: x. Explanation: In linear regression, x is the independent (predictor) variable — the one used to make predictions. y is the dependent variable whose value is predicted based on x. 'm' is the slope and 'b' is the y-intercept.

questions.question: What is the purpose of data cleaning in the data analysis process? ★

options.B: To remove duplicate values, fix errors, and handle missing data to improve data quality
options.C: To select which statistical model to use
options.D: To collect additional data from external sources

questions.explanation: To remove duplicate values, fix errors, and handle missing data to improve data quality. Explanation: Data cleaning (also called data wrangling) ensures the dataset is accurate and consistent before analysis. Poor quality data leads to unreliable conclusions — 'garbage in, garbage out.'

questions.question: Which of the following platforms is commonly used to download publicly available datasets for data analysis? ★

options.B: Kaggle
options.C: Adobe Photoshop

questions.explanation: Kaggle. Explanation: Kaggle (www.kaggle.com) is a widely used platform that hosts thousands of publicly available datasets for machine learning, data analysis, and competitions. GitHub is also commonly used for dataset sharing.

questions.question: What does the pandas function data.head(10) do in Python? ★

options.A: Deletes the first 10 rows of the dataset
options.B: Displays the first 10 rows of the dataset
options.C: Sorts the dataset by the first 10 columns
options.D: Counts the number of rows up to 10

questions.explanation: Displays the first 10 rows of the dataset. Explanation: The .head(n) function in Pandas returns the first n rows of a DataFrame. It is commonly used at the start of data analysis to quickly inspect the structure and content of the dataset.

questions.question: A scatter plot is most useful for: ★

options.A: Showing the proportion of categories in a whole
options.B: Displaying frequency distributions of a single variable
options.C: Visualizing the relationship or correlation between two numerical variables

questions.explanation: Visualizing the relationship or correlation between two numerical variables. Explanation: A scatter plot places each data point at coordinates (x, y) representing two variables. The resulting pattern reveals whether the variables are positively correlated, negatively correlated, or unrelated.

questions.question: What does the term 'dispersion' refer to in summary statistics? ★

options.A: How closely similar the data values are to each other (central tendency)
options.B: How spread out or scattered the data values are from the average
options.C: The most frequently occurring value
options.D: The total number of data points

questions.explanation: How spread out or scattered the data values are from the average. Explanation: Dispersion measures describe how spread out data is. Key dispersion measures include range, variance, and standard deviation. High dispersion means data is widely scattered; low dispersion means it is tightly grouped.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a real-world data science use case mentioned in the textbook? ★

options.B: Weather forecasting using predictive analysis
options.C: Writing a Python function

questions.explanation: Weather forecasting using predictive analysis. Explanation: Weather forecasting is a classic real-world data science use case — historical data on temperature, rainfall, wind speed, and pressure is collected, cleaned, and fitted to statistical models to predict future weather conditions.

questions.question: What is the range of the dataset {12, 7, 25, 3, 19}? ★
questions.explanation: 22. Explanation: Range = Maximum value - Minimum value = 25 - 3 = 22. The range is the simplest measure of dispersion and shows the total spread of the dataset.

questions.question: In the context of data science, what does KPI stand for and why is it important? ★

options.A: Key Processing Index — measures CPU speed
options.B: Key Performance Indicator — measures the success of a data science project against defined goals
options.C: Knowledge Processing Intelligence — tracks AI accuracy
options.D: Kernel Python Interface — manages data imports

questions.explanation: Key Performance Indicator — measures the success of a data science project against defined goals. Explanation: KPIs are measurable values defined at the start of a data science project to evaluate whether goals are being met. Defining KPIs upfront ensures that the project stays focused and its results can be objectively evaluated.
